subject: Metrics exposure policy & temporary SLO exemption request
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearlane.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearLane Procurement Team <procurement@clearlane.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: how you measure uptime/latency + temporary visibility for onboarding

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the engineering team was impressed with the throughput. Procurement has a few narrow follow-ups for our internal risk assessment before we sign the SOW. Can you confirm the following in writing? We need these items attached to the procurement record (DL-4931):

1) How Redwood defines and calculates uptime for hosted deployments (lookback window, numerator/denominator, excluded windows).
2) How latency SLOs are measured (p50/p95/p99 definitions, cold-start handling, measurement point).
3) What monitoring/alerting tooling you provide to customers (dashboards, alert channels, sampling).
4) Whether we can get read-only dashboard access and for how long during onboarding (temporary exception policy).
5) Evidence artefacts you can provide (dashboard snapshots, metrics CSVs, runbooks).

We may ask for a 30-day temporary visibility window into a scoped set of dashboards while our integration team validates performance. Please reply with the measurement definitions and a proposal for a temporary access plan and any security controls you require.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
ClearLane Logistics
[Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: how you measure uptime/latency + temporary visibility for onboarding

Hi Alyssa — great question, thanks for outlining this clearly. Summary below; attaching a short instrumentation matrix and our uptime spec for reference. Vivek and Marcus are looped in for the technical details and to propose the access workflow.

Quick answers (high level):
- Uptime: calculated as successful 2xx responses / total requests for the control-plane tenant endpoint over a rolling 30-day window with a standard 99.9% target in the SOW. We exclude planned maintenance windows and certified outages (we provide notifications).
- Latency SLOs: we measure at the edge (gateway) post-auth, and report p50/p95/p99 for server-generated tokens. Cold-starts (container spin-up) are excluded from standard SLO reporting but flagged separately in the instrumentation.
- Monitoring: we provide Grafana dashboards (read-only), Prometheus-style metrics ingestion, and alerting via PagerDuty/SNS. Sampling is adjustable per account; default is full request sampling for error rate and 1/10 sampling for token-level traces.
- Temporary access: we can grant a scoped read-only Grafana invite for a 30-day onboarding window; we require an approved list of viewer emails and will create an API token with restricted scopes.
- Evidence: exports include dashboard snapshots, CSV time series for the measured metrics, and runbook excerpts.

Next steps: Vivek, can you confirm the exact metric names, the retention window for raw metrics, and the proposed conservative read-only scope (dashboards + metrics API) so I can confirm with Alyssa? Marcus, please add any compliance notes about PD/SSO requirements.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-instrumentation-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: how you measure uptime/latency + temporary visibility for onboarding

Hi Monica / Alyssa — technical follow-up below, pasted into bullets for procurement. If you need a short walkthrough call I can join.

1) Uptime calculation (documentation attached as uptime-calculation-spec.pdf):
   - Metric: redwood_service_request_success_ratio{tenant="clearlane"}
   - Numerator: count(status>=200 and status<400) over window
   - Denominator: total request count over same window
   - Window: rolling 30 days; SLA reported monthly using UTC day boundaries.
   - Exclusions: planned maintenance (announced in advance), emergency maintenance windows approved by both parties, and upstream provider outages where we have documented evidence.

2) Latency measurement:
   - Measurement point: edge gateway post-auth (this captures network + service processing).
   - Buckets: p50/p95/p99 computed on request duration in milliseconds using summary metric redwood_request_duration_ms_bucket.
   - Cold starts: identified by instance boot events; any request with instance_age < 30s is tagged as cold_start=true and excluded from the SLO percentile computation. Cold-start counts are surfaced in a separate metric redwood_cold_start_count.

3) Monitoring / alerting capabilities:
   - Dashboards: per-tenant Grafana dashboards (SLO overview, latency distribution, error budget burn, KPIs).
   - Alerts: we run alert rules in Grafana/Alertmanager; standard thresholds are: error_rate > 0.1% sustained for 5m triggers P2; p95 latency above 800ms sustained for 10m triggers P2.
   - Channels: PagerDuty, webhook, email — configured per account.
   - Retention: aggregated metrics (1m granularity) retained for 13 months; raw request logs retained for 90 days by default.

4) Read-only access proposal (temporary onboarding exception):
   - Scope: read-only Grafana access limited to two dashboards (SLO overview, latency heatmap) + a metrics API token that allows metrics:read for tenant=clearlane. No logs or traces by default.
   - Duration: 30 calendar days (can be shortened).
   - Security: must use company email (SSO enforced); IP allowlist optional for higher sensitivity accounts; API token expiry enforced at 30 days.
   - Auditing: we will provide an access log extract showing viewer emails and timestamps for the period.

5) Evidence: we can supply: dashboard PNG exports (per day), CSV time-series for the metrics above (by day/hour), confirmation of alert rules, and the runbook snippet that describes incident triage.

Attachments: uptime-calculation-spec.pdf

If this matches what you need, Monica — I can prepare the Grafana invite and a metrics CSV export of the last 90 days to attach to the procurement packet.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Engineer, Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: how you measure uptime/latency + temporary visibility for onboarding

Alyssa / Monica — quick compliance notes from my side:

- SSO: We require SAML/OIDC SSO for any account with read-only dashboard access. If ClearLane cannot support SSO for the 30-day window, we can issue time-limited invites tied to company emails but will need a secondary approver in procurement.
- Data access scope: no PII is exposed via the suggested dashboards; traces/logs are excluded unless you request them specifically and sign the additional data access amendment.
- Audit trail: we keep a tamper-evident audit log for the period of access and can export it to you for the procurement record.

I can also provide a signed attestation that the temporary access will be disabled automatically at expiry date.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
